# Synthetic document-stack fixtures

These documents contain no customer data. They exercise the actual HTTP upload,
durable queue, worker, saved artifact, and download/rescan boundaries in
`scripts/verify_document_stack.ts`.

- `course.pptx`: a title slide, "Course overview", with grey text on white.
  Expected deterministic contrast remediation: scanner score 92 to 100.
- `course.xlsx`: Course/Credits headings and one History/3 row. Expected
  deterministic workbook remediation: scanner score 49 to 100.
- `course.docx`: a level-two "Course overview" heading followed by eight-point
  "Tiny body text". Manual work remains, so the worker must withhold output and
  retain every original finding in unresolved totals.

- `metadata.pdf`: generated by the existing `scripts/pdf_acceptance_corpus.py`
  metadata case. The full raw scan, rather than a filtered issue subset, must
  produce a downloaded and rescanned artifact; extracted text remains unchanged.

The PDF refusal case uses the existing `pdfs/simple_syllabus.pdf` fixture. A passing
scanner score is not an accessibility conformance certification. PDF semantic
regression tests separately compare source and output checkpoint results.
